module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 214

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/214](https://www.erdosproblems.com/214)
- [CsTo94] Csizmadia, György and Tóth, Géza, *Note on a Ramsey-type problem in geometry*.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1994), 302-306.
- [EGMRSS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Montgomery, P. and Rothschild, B. L. and Spencer, J.
  and Straus, E. G., *Euclidean Ramsey theorems. II*. (1975), 529-557.
- [Ju79] Juhász, Rozália, *Ramsey type theorems in the plane*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1979),
  152-160.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Congruent EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos214

/-- The four vertices of a unit square. -/
def unitSquare : Fin 4 → ℝ² := ![!₂[0, 0], !₂[1, 0], !₂[1, 1], !₂[0, 1]]

/-- Colouring the points of `S` blue and the points of `Sᶜ` red gives a red/blue colouring of
$\mathbb{R}^2$; it is unit-distance-avoiding if no two blue points are distance $1$ apart. -/
def UnitDistanceAvoiding (S : Set ℝ²) : Prop := ∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, dist x y ≠ 1

/-- Any unit-distance-avoiding colouring contains a congruent red copy of every set of `n`
points. -/
def HasRedCopies (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set ℝ², UnitDistanceAvoiding S → ∀ K : Fin n → ℝ², Function.Injective K →
    ∃ p : Fin n → ℝ², (∀ i, p i ∈ Sᶜ) ∧ (p ≅ K)

/-- The largest integer `k` such that any unit-distance-avoiding colouring contains a congruent
red copy of every set of `k` points. -/
noncomputable def k : ℕ := sSup {n | HasRedCopies n}

/--
Let $S\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be such that no two points in $S$ are distance $1$ apart. Must the
complement of $S$ contain four points which form a unit square?

The answer is yes, proved by Juhász [Ju79], who proved more generally that the complement of $S$
must contain a congruent copy of any set of four points.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos214.lean"]
theorem erdos_214 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ S : Set ℝ², UnitDistanceAvoiding S →
      ∃ p : Fin 4 → ℝ², (∀ i, p i ∈ Sᶜ) ∧ (p ≅ unitSquare) := by
  sorry

/--
The answer is yes, proved by Juhász [Ju79], who proved more generally that the complement of $S$
must contain a congruent copy of any set of four points.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_214.variants.juhasz : HasRedCopies 4 := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer, and Straus [EGMRSS75] had earlier showed that
$3\leq k\leq 10^{12}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_214.variants.egmrss : 3 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ 10 ^ 12 := by
  sorry

/--
Juhász [Ju79] also improved the upper bound to $k\leq 11$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_214.variants.juhasz_twelve_points : ¬ HasRedCopies 12 := by
  sorry

/--
The upper bound was improved further by Csizmadia and Tóth [CsTo94] to $k\leq 7$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_214.variants.csizmadia_toth : ¬ HasRedCopies 8 := by
  sorry

/--
The best known bounds currently are
$$4\leq k\leq 7.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_214.variants.bounds : 4 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ 7 := by
  sorry

end Erdos214

reformulations.difference: The source's k is "the largest integer such that any such colouring contains a congruent red copy of every set of k points". The Lean defines `k := sSup {n | HasRedCopies n}` on ℕ, which returns the junk value 0 when the set is unbounded. `egmrss` (`3 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ 10^12`) and `bounds` (`4 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ 7`) are stated through this `sSup`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: In a scratch file I proved in Lean that `HasRedCopies` is downward closed: given an injective K : Fin n → ℝ², extend it with `Fin.snoc` by a point outside its finite range, then restrict the red copy. The set also contains 0. So `sSup` is the largest element whenever the set is bounded, and the 8-point counterexample (Csizmadia–Tóth) bounds it; the junk value is never reached. I also proved `(a ≤ k ∧ k ≤ b) ↔ (HasRedCopies a ∧ ¬ HasRedCopies (b+1))` for every `1 ≤ a`. Hence `egmrss` ↔ `HasRedCopies 3 ∧ ¬HasRedCopies (10^12+1)` and `bounds` ↔ `HasRedCopies 4 ∧ ¬HasRedCopies 8`. These are exactly the source's "3 ≤ k ≤ 10^12" and "4 ≤ k ≤ 7" for the largest such integer. EGMRSS75's Theorem 3 (every 3-point set has a translate in the other colour) and its 10^12-point counterexample together imply the Lean `egmrss`.

reformulations.difference: The source says "Juhász also improved the upper bound to k ≤ 11". The Lean states `¬ HasRedCopies 12` rather than an inequality on `k`. `erdos_214.variants.csizmadia_toth` does the same: `¬ HasRedCopies 8` for "k ≤ 7".
reformulations.equivalence_argument: I proved in Lean that `¬ HasRedCopies (b+1) ↔ (BddAbove {n | HasRedCopies n} ∧ k ≤ b)`, using the downward closure proved in the same scratch file. So the Lean form says exactly that the largest such integer exists and is at most b, which is the source's claim; a bare `k ≤ b` would be weaker only because of the `sSup` junk value. The Lean form is also literally the theorems proved: Juhász's Theorem 2 gives a 12-point configuration and a unit-distance-avoiding colouring in which every congruent copy has a point of the avoiding colour. Csizmadia–Tóth's Theorem 1 does the same with 8 points (a regular heptagon of circumradius 0.9 plus its centre). Their colour names are swapped relative to the file, but the roles match `S`/`Sᶜ`.

review.notes:
No findings. The source (erdosproblems.com/214, last edited 2 April 2026, status "PROVED (LEAN)") says: "Let S ⊂ ℝ² be such that no two points in S are distance 1 apart. Must the complement of S contain four points which form a unit square? ... Call a red/blue colouring of ℝ² unit-distance-avoiding if no two blue points are distance 1 apart. Let k be the largest integer such that any such colouring contains a congruent red copy of every set of k points ... [EGMRSS75] 3 ≤ k ≤ 10^12 ... [Ju79] k ≤ 11 ... [CsTo94] k ≤ 7 ... best known bounds 4 ≤ k ≤ 7." Each declaration matches this text.

- `erdos_214` asks for a red congruent copy of the unit square for every unit-distance-avoiding S. The main theorem correctly uses `answer(True)`. I checked in Lean that the metric is Euclidean (side 1, diagonal √2) and that `unitSquare` is injective.
- `juhasz` is `HasRedCopies 4`.
- The variants are faithful; see the reformulations for the `sSup` encoding and the `¬HasRedCopies` form of the upper bounds, both proved in Lean.

Boundary cases:
- S = ∅ is allowed and is trivial.
- `HasRedCopies 0` holds.
- The junk value of `k` (`sSup` of an unbounded set is 0) cannot be reached, because the set is bounded.
- `Congruent` means equal pairwise distances, which in ℝ² is the same as an isometric image. This matches "congruent" in the papers, reflections included.

Minor observations, none of them defects:
- EGMRSS75 actually gives k ≤ 10^12 − 1, since its counterexample has exactly 10^12 points. The source and the Lean both state the slightly weaker `k ≤ 10^12`, which is true.
- The formal-proof file cited on `erdos_214` also proves the `juhasz` variant (theorem_1) and the `juhasz_twelve_points` variant (theorem_2). Neither variant carries a `formal_proof` attribute. This is optional metadata and contradicts nothing.
- The original Erdős reference [Er83c, p. 47] is not in the module docstring.
- I could not get the Juhász 1979 full text (ScienceDirect and S3 blocked). Her two results are confirmed by the Csizmadia–Tóth introduction, the source page, the forum comment, and the two Lean formalizations of her Theorems 1 and 2.

Status: all six declarations are tagged `research solved`, which matches the source. The `formal_proof` link resolves and proves the statement.
